title: Idempotent leading coefficient of a commuting idempotent determinant
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $J$ a finite set, and $T,P\in\operatorname{Mat}_J(A)$ with $P^2=P$ and $TP=PT$. Let $D(T,P)$ be the polynomial of [def-weil-pbc-idempotent-charpoly]. Its leading coefficient $c$ satisfies $c^2=c$.

source.place: Tag 09XI, lemma-characterize-henselian-pair, proof of (3) implies (1), splitting and characteristic-polynomial paragraphs; matrix formula and omitted details written out by G2

proof.text: Reindex the finite ambient module by Fin of its cardinality. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-idempotent-endomorphism-image-base-change] to P and 1-P to obtain complementary finite projective images, whose split decomposition persists under localization. Choose finite standard free covers for both images using [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-standard-free-cover], and refine to the product cover. Each summand is finite free on each refined localization. The products still generate the unit ideal, by multiplying the two expressions for 1 in the two original generated ideals.

Commutation with P makes T preserve both summands. In the concatenation of their bases, P is diag(1,0), T is block diagonal and the matrix defining D(T,P) [def-weil-pbc-idempotent-charpoly] is diag(X-T_image,1). Determinant base change and basis invariance identify its localized determinant with the characteristic polynomial on the first summand. By [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-free-module-properties], it is monic of degree r, the rank of that summand, on every nonzero localization.

Put d=natDegree D(T,P). Polynomial degree cannot increase under a ring map: all coefficients above d remain zero. Thus each local degree r is at most d. The image of the global coefficient at d is 1 when r=d, and 0 when r<d, by the local monicity and vanishing of coefficients above the local degree. It is therefore idempotent in every nonzero cover localization. In zero localizations the idempotence equation is automatic.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localized-span-eq-zero] with module A to the element c*c-c, where c is the leading coefficient, on the refined standard cover. Every localized image is zero by the previous step, hence c*c-c=0 over A. For A the zero ring this equation is automatic.
